title: Variant safety passport and explainable regression harness for quantized onboarding
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Create a machine-readable 'Variant Safety Passport' artifact and an associated explainable regression harness for onboarding INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ model variants. The passport consolidates performance, cost, memory, deterministic stability, and failure-mode signals so downstream systems (pinning, release gating, Console UI) can make informed decisions. The harness performs targeted, explainable regressions on acceptance prompts and synthetic stress inputs and produces a delta report that maps regressions to likely root causes (kernel mismatch, quant rounding, KV divergence).

Scope and non-goals:
- In-scope: artifact schema, CI canary job, metric definitions, explainability traces, integration with the quant artifact registry, dashboarding, and CI gating.
- Out-of-scope: full automation of rollback policies (separate rollback orchestration epic) and human-in-the-loop triage UI (Console changes will be a follow-up).

Why this matters: We've onboarded many low-precision variants, but regressions are often opaque: teams see a delta score and must laboriously reproduce failures. This ticket standardizes the artifact emitted on publish and gives engineers and PMs a minimal, explainable failure breadcrumb trail so pinning/rollback decisions can be automated or fast-tracked.
acceptance_criteria: Define Variant Safety Passport JSON schema and store examples for INT8, GPTQ, AWQ and FP8 variants in the artifact registry.
CI canary job that runs 500 prompt samples + 100 stress perturbations for each candidate variant and emits a regression delta report in <30m for small models (<8B).

Delta report includes: p50/p95 latency, token-level divergence heatmap, top-5 failing prompts with reproducible seeds, likely root-cause tags (kernel/memory/quantization-noise), and suggested rollback score thresholds.
Publish pipeline refuses to promote a variant if regression score > 1.5% MFT accuracy drop or > 10% increase in p95 latency; thresholds configurable via release-1.22 feature flags.
Telemetry: mapped Grafana dashboard (link in comments) shows baseline vs variant trends and exposes the Passport fields for ops teams.
Documented runbook for triage attached to the Confluence page and linked from the artifact metadata.
Security review signoff obtained for artifact persistence and passenger data retention (KMS/roles confirmed).
tasks: Draft Variant Safety Passport schema (fields: model_key, variant_key, quant_type, footprint_gb, expected_throughput_rps, latency_p50_p95, pass_rate_on_eval_suite, token_divergence_samples, explain_traces_link, publish_timestamp)
Implement canary runner that executes seeded generation on the canonical prompt set + perturbations set and writes delta report to artifact registry
Add explainability traces: record KV cache checksums per layer, per-token logits/entropy delta for top-k tokens
Integrate CI gate: fail publish job if regression guards trip; add opt-out tag for experimental internal-only variants
Schema validators and unit tests for passport ingestion in console and pin service
Create Grafana dashboard panels and an alert for +regression spikes (>3 failing prompts in last 24h)
Confluence doc with triage steps, sample commands, and example investigations
Security review: ensure artifact blob encryption and RBAC for access; list retention policy
notes: We borrowed concept 'safety passport' from feature flags used in other infra teams but extended it to include explainability traces specific to low-precision failure modes.
The passport is intentionally compact so it can be attached to pinned versions without blowing up storage budgets; heavy trace artifacts are stored behind TTL and a pointer lives in the passport.
We will initially gate only on MFT-style accuracy delta and latency; later iterations will add embedding drift and hallucination proxies.
Decision: default canary sample size set to 500/100 after benchmarking on small models; scale target sample size by model parameter count in follow-on ticket.
